sections.html:
Kearns is a city on the west side of the Salt Lake Valley, bordered by West Valley City to the north and west, Taylorsville to the east and West Jordan to the south. It covers 4.63 square miles, all land, at an elevation of about 4,530 feet.

Most of Kearns sits on the old bed of Lake Bonneville, the ancient lake that once filled the valley. A low rise called the Kearns-Benion hill climbs about 100 feet above the valley floor and runs northwest from the Jordan River toward the Oquirrh Mountains.

With a density of nearly 8,000 people per square mile, Kearns is a compact place where houses sit close together, and a vacant or neglected one is easy to notice from the street.

sections.h2: How did an Army base become Kearns?
sections.html:
Kearns began on May 1, 1942, as Kearns Army Air Base, a World War II training facility for the U.S. Army Air Forces named for Utah Senator Thomas Kearns. The land before then was dry farmland that had been set aside for universities and colleges.

The base was renamed Camp Kearns on January 1, 1944, and it was deactivated on August 15, 1946, when the Air Force transferred it to the State of Utah. Developers then built homes and businesses on the former base land, and Kearns grew into what Wikipedia calls the first suburb in Salt Lake County.

  • The base's streets and building foundations served as a template for the new neighborhoods.
  • A base chapel became part of Our Lady of Perpetual Help Catholic Church.
  • A base train station later served as a day-care center.
  • A base theater became part of Kearns Junior High School.

For sellers, the postwar origin matters. Kearns grew quickly in the mid to late 20th century, so a seller with a house from that era may be dealing with original roofs, wiring and plumbing. Population grew to 17,172 in 1960 and 21,353 by 1980, with later development reaching west of the railroad tracks to 5600 West.

sections.h2: How did Kearns become a city?
sections.html:
Kearns became an incorporated city on May 1, 2024, under Utah House Bill 35, after years as an unincorporated community, a township and a metro township. Township status came on June 1, 2002, and voters approved a metro township in 2015, with that government taking effect January 1, 2017.

Residents resisted annexation by West Valley City and West Jordan during the 1990s, collecting enough signatures to keep the boundaries unchanged. Jesse Valdez is the first elected mayor of the City of Kearns. The mayor's office is at 4250 W 5415 S, by appointment, and the phone is 385-855-8375.

Day-to-day services still run through shared providers. Police and fire come through Unified Police and Unified Fire, and the Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District handles building permits, business licensing, land use and zoning, code enforcement and stormwater. The district is at 860 W. Levoy Dr., Suite 300, Taylorsville, and its main number is 385-910-5600.

Coverage in the Taylorsville Journal said the city gained more tax options as a result, including a property tax and a telecommunications tax, and planned to create a redevelopment agency. Sellers who care about future taxes can watch the city's budget and agenda pages.

sections.h2: What is the Utah Olympic Oval, and why is it in Kearns?
sections.html:
The Utah Olympic Oval is a five-acre ice sports facility at 5662 South Cougar Lane in Kearns, built in 2001 for the 2002 Winter Olympics. It has Utah's only 400-meter speed skating oval, two international-size ice sheets and a four-lane, 442-meter running track.

It sits in Oquirrh Park, and the Oquirrh Recreation and Parks District runs the surrounding fitness center and programs, including public skating, Learn to Skate classes and curling. Kearns has also kept an annual parade each late July or early August, and a new Kearns Library opened in December 2020.

The Oval is a public venue as well as a former Olympic site, and the district lists skate rentals for people without their own skates.

sections.h2: Which schools and local landmarks serve Kearns?
sections.html:
Kearns is in the Granite School District, which also serves Holladay, West Valley City, Taylorsville and other Salt Lake County communities, and Kearns High School serves the city. Kearns Junior High School includes the former base theater.

South Valley Regional Airport, which began as Municipal Airport No. 2 near the base, was a small private-aviation field on the south border of the old base.

sections.h2: What does the Salt Lake Valley climate mean for a Kearns house?
sections.html:
Kearns has a humid continental climate, with warm and usually dry summers, cold winters and large seasonal swings. Salt Lake County gets about 15 inches of precipitation and 55 inches of snow in a typical year, and winter temperature inversions can trap pollution in the valley.

Snow and long cold stretches put the roof and heating system to work each winter, and a seller who knows their ages is ready for the first question a buyer asks.

Earthquakes are the other concern. The Wasatch fault is Utah's most active, and the Utah Geological Survey says liquefaction is most likely in low-lying central parts of a valley, especially near lakes and stream corridors where groundwater is shallow. Susceptible soils are loose, young, sandy or silty deposits that are saturated within about 30 to 50 feet of the surface. Because Kearns lies on the Bonneville lake bed, a lot-specific check on the survey's maps makes sense.

  • Maps show general patterns only.
  • A site study by a Utah-licensed engineer and geologist is needed for any one lot.
  • The last large quake on the Salt Lake City segment was about 1,400 years ago.

sections.h2: How do property tax dates work for a Kearns house?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County collects property tax on Kearns houses, and the bill is due November 30, with delinquency starting December 1. The county values property as of January 1.

The Board of Equalization looks only at current-year market value, and taxes remain due while an appeal is pending. The county accepts evidence such as a recent purchase, a fee appraisal, or three to five comparable sales. Relief programs run through the Treasurer at 385-468-8300.

A Kearns house that was the owner's primary residence is taxed on 55% of its value because of the 45% primary residential exemption. The exemption requires occupancy for at least 183 consecutive days in a year, and a new owner has to file a fresh claim after the sale.

sections.h2: What does it take to close a cash sale in Kearns?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Kearns closes at a title or escrow company, and the deed is recorded with the Salt Lake County Recorder at 2001 South State Street. The recorder's flat fee was $40 under the October 2024 schedule, and it requires a Salt Lake County legal description, the parcel number and an original notarized signature.

  • The grantee's mailing address must appear on the deed.
  • The paper must be white, 8.5 by 11 inches, with a clear space at the top of the first page.
  • Original documents come back by mail two to three weeks after processing.
  • The Recorder does not prepare or notarize documents, and the phone is 385-468-8145.

Title companies normally handle these details, but a seller should still check that the names on the deed match the names on the signature page.

sections.h2: What do Kearns sellers usually deal with?
sections.html:
Kearns sellers choose between listing, a private sale and a cash offer. Listing involves preparing the house, paying commission and waiting for a buyer's loan, while a cash sale lets the house sell in its present state with a closing date the seller helps choose.

  • Houses from the postwar decades with original systems that need replacing.
  • Inherited homes where the family is in no position to repair them.
  • Rentals with tenants who make showings hard to arrange.
  • Owners facing missed payments who need a firm closing timeline.

Whatever the route, get the closing date and proof of funds in writing, and compare any offer against a listing's net after repairs and commission.

faqs.q: Is Kearns a city or a township?
faqs.a: Kearns is a city. It became an incorporated city on May 1, 2024, after serving as a township and then a metro township. Many services are still provided through the Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District.

faqs.q: Who handles building permits in Kearns?
faqs.a: The Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District handles building permits, business licensing, land use, zoning, code enforcement and stormwater for Kearns. Its main number is 385-910-5600.

faqs.q: What is the property tax deadline in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: November 30. Taxes become delinquent on December 1. The 2026 appeal window ran from July 31 to September 15.

faqs.q: Does Kearns have its own police and fire department?
faqs.a: Police and fire service come from Unified Police and Unified Fire, according to a May 2024 report on the city's incorporation.

faqs.q: How many people live in Kearns?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 36,723, and the Census Bureau estimates 35,404 for July 1, 2025.
